preconditions.description: The integer n is the count of logical arguments and satisfies 1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000.

preconditions.expression: all(a_i in {0, 1} for a_i in a)
preconditions.description: Each a_i in the input sequence a is either 0 (false) or 1 (true).
The input sequence a has exactly n elements.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'NO' or (stdout == 'YES' and '(' in expression and ')' in expression and '->' in expression)
postconditions.description: If no valid bracketing exists to make the expression evaluate to false, output 'NO'. Otherwise, output 'YES' followed by a valid bracketed expression that evaluates to false.
The bracketed expression (if provided) must evaluate to false (0) when parsed with left-associative implication rules and brackets.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'NO' or (stdout == 'YES' and all(c in {'0', '1', '(', ')', '-', '>'} for c in expression))
postconditions.description: The output expression (if provided) contains only valid characters: '0', '1', '(', ')', '-', '>' (paired as '->').
The length of the output expression (if provided) does not exceed 1,000,000 characters.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'NO' or (stdout == 'YES' and ''.join(str(a_i) for a_i in a) == ''.join(c for c in expression if c in {'0', '1'}))
postconditions.description: The sequence of digits in the output expression (if provided) matches the input sequence a in order.
